pr.title: Optionally fuse padding in MXFP8 quantize kernel
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`mxfp8_quantize(..., backend="cute-dsl")` with the linear scale layout pads K up to `alignment` on the host: it allocates `torch.zeros(m, padded_k)`, copies the input into it, and quantizes the padded copy. That is two extra passes over the activations (a memset and a copy) for columns that only ever become zeros. This shows up wherever a hidden size is padded for a block-scaled GEMM. For example, vLLM's gpt-oss MoE backend that runs FlashInfer's TRT-LLM kernels with MXFP8 activations (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`) quantizes the MoE input through this path with the linear layout and `alignment=256`, padding the 2880-wide hidden states to 3072 in every MoE layer.

This PR moves the padding into `MXFP8QuantizeLinearKernel`, which now reads the unpadded `[M, K]` input and writes the padded `[M, padded_K]` output and scales itself:

- When `K < padded_K`, 15 of the CTA's 16 warps quantize the input's scale blocks; the last warp writes the zero FP8 columns `[K, padded_K)` (8-byte stores) and the zero scale bytes of every row its CTA owns. The block keeps its 512 threads.
- An all-zero 32-element block quantizes to FP8 zero with scale 0, so the output is byte-identical to quantizing the zero-padded copy.
- Scales are indexed per output row (`row * padded_K/32 + col`) instead of by the flat block index.
- The kernel is compiled per `(K, dtype, pdl, use_2t, padded_K)`. When `K == padded_K` it is the same kernel as before. Swizzled layouts (128x4, 8x4) are unchanged and still pad on the host.
- No new input constraints: K and `alignment` must already be multiples of 32, which keeps the 8-byte zero stores aligned.

A second commit fixes `benchmarks/routines/quantization.py` so the `mxfp8_quantize` routine can measure this case. It required `k % alignment == 0` (treating `--alignment` as the scale vector size), so any K that `mxfp8_quantize` would pad was rejected. It now checks K and `--alignment` against 32, compares only the first K columns in `--refcheck`, and counts the padded output bytes in the bandwidth figure.

### Performance

B200, bf16 input, linear scale layout, PDL off. Median of 3 runs per tree, alternating, on the same GPU.

`python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine mxfp8_quantize --m <M> --k <K> --alignment <A> --no_sf_swizzled_layout --backends cute-dsl --input_dtype bfloat16 --num_iters 1000 --dry_run_iters 100`

This times the whole call, including the host-side pad on main, in a CUDA graph with rotating input buffers (cold L2), using CUDA events (`cupti-python` was not installed). "main" is main plus only the benchmark fix, since main's routine rejects these shapes. The `cuda` backend column is for reference; this PR does not touch it.

`alignment=128`:

| M | K → padded K | main, cute-dsl (µs) | this PR, cute-dsl (µs) | speedup | cuda backend (µs) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2880 → 2944 | 3.85 | 1.80 | 2.1x | 2.82 |
| 8 | 2880 → 2944 | 4.66 | 1.80 | 2.6x | 3.02 |
| 64 | 2880 → 2944 | 5.07 | 1.80 | 2.8x | 3.03 |
| 512 | 2880 → 2944 | 7.74 | 2.62 | 3.0x | 3.44 |
| 2048 | 2880 → 2944 | 22.29 | 4.87 | 4.6x | 5.90 |
| 8192 | 2880 → 2944 | 77.17 | 13.27 | 5.8x | 18.60 |
| 2048 | 1568 → 1664 | 12.46 | 3.22 | 3.9x | 4.65 |
| 2048 | 4000 → 4096 | 29.25 | 6.09 | 4.8x | 6.52 |

`alignment=256`, as in the vLLM path above (K = 2880 → 3072):

| M | main, cute-dsl (µs) | this PR, cute-dsl (µs) | speedup | cuda backend (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.64 | 1.80 | 2.0x | 2.82 |
| 8 | 4.67 | 1.80 | 2.6x | 3.03 |
| 64 | 4.87 | 1.80 | 2.7x | 3.03 |
| 512 | 7.74 | 2.62 | 3.0x | 3.44 |
| 2048 | 22.47 | 4.85 | 4.6x | 5.90 |
| 8192 | 78.60 | 13.27 | 5.9x | 17.77 |

Before this PR the padded cute-dsl path was slower than the `cuda` backend at every shape in both tables; with it, it is faster at every one. Calls whose K is already a multiple of `alignment` run the same kernel as before.

### Testing

- New `tests/utils/test_fp8_quantize.py::test_mxfp8_quantize_cute_dsl_linear_pads_in_kernel`: 180 cases (M = 1, 3, 127, 1024, 8192; K/alignment = 2880/128, 2880/256, 96/128, 32/256, 1056/1024, 4064/4096; fp16/bf16/fp32; PDL on/off). Each compares the output byte for byte, padding included, with quantizing an explicitly zero-padded input, after poisoning the caching allocator with 0xFF so unwritten padding would show. With the zero-fill warp disabled, all 180 fail.
- The existing `test_mxfp8_quantize_alignment_torch_device` (linear and swizzled, K = 1568, alignment 64 and 128) exercises this path as well.
- On B200, `pytest tests/utils/test_fp8_quantize.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_dispatch.py`: 1290 passed, 185 skipped, 0 failed. `flashinfer_benchmark.py --refcheck` on the padded shapes (K = 2880 and 1568 at alignment 128, K = 2880 at alignment 256) finds 0 mismatched elements for both the `cuda` and `cute-dsl` backends.

- The kernel change is confined to the `has_pad` branches in `MXFP8QuantizeLinearKernel` (the warp split, the zero-fill loop) and the scale index; with `K == padded_K` the generated kernel is unchanged.
